text:
marco: FYI incident summary & required actions — a third-party analytics integration (vendor: StatTrace) was found sending our service API key in request bodies to their ingestion endpoint. We believe the key was copied into an environment var on one staging service and the integration forwarded it in a debug payload. No customer PII found, but this is a production key and needs rotation asap.

alisha: How did we detect this? Any sign of exfil beyond vendor logs?

marco: We detected it via a sudden spike in outbound TLS hosts to stattrace.com from a staging pool and a pattern match in recent egress logs. Vendor confirmed the key appeared in their request logs for a ~2h window. We don't have evidence the key was shared beyond StatTrace, but treat as compromised for now.

lina: Which key(s) specifically? Service account vs API tokens?

marco: A long-lived service API key associated with the "model-proxy" service (scoped to read/write inference-logs). Identifier: redwood:model-proxy:prod:key-7. Owner: @alisha.

integrations: We've paused the StatTrace integration ingest and requested log retention/export. They'll provide a redacted copy of the offending requests.

ops-oncall: Immediate actions we're initiating: 1) rotate the service key (we will create a new key and revoke the old) for any keys we manage that are flagged; 2) run a targeted search for other services that exported keys to external hosts; 3) block egress to stattrace.com from prod until confirmed safe. ETA 2h for rotation rollout.

marco: Required actions for owners (this is mandatory): 1) Confirm you own the key under SEC-3301 and update the ticket with which services use the new key (include deploy tags). 2) Rotate and replace the key in your service config (dont reuse the same secret). 3) Confirm no infra automation commits the raw key into vendor config. 4) Add a least-privilege scope if the key currently allows write when read would suffice.

alisha: I'm on it. Will rotate and push a new key to our secret manager, then update the ticket. What's the deadline?

marco: Deadline: EOD tomorrow UTC. If you cannot meet it, escalate to @ops-oncall now. We will auto-revoke the old key 24h after new issuance unless you request exception in SEC-3301.

sec-bot: Created SEC-3301 and linked to this thread. Scheduled automated egress block and key-rotation task for affected managed keys. If you are an affected owner and need help, reply here or DM @marco.

lina: Any mitigation steps for apps that can't rotate immediately?

ops-oncall: We can issue short-lived proxy tokens as a bridge. Steps: 1) create new short-lived key via console (TTL 1h) 2) update service to use proxy token and schedule rolling deploy. Use this only as emergency: https://redwood.internal/docs/keys/shortlived.

marco: Hunting queries (run in internal SIEM):

```sql
-- find egress flows to stattrace within window
SELECT src_service, dst_host, timestamp, request_path
FROM egress_logs
WHERE dst_host LIKE '%stattrace.com%'
  AND timestamp >= '2026-03-20T08:00:00Z'
  AND timestamp <= '2026-03-20T10:30:00Z';
```

marco: Please paste your rotation proof into SEC-3301 (export of deploy tag or secret-manager version). We'll audit all managed keys and force-rotate ones we own. For user-managed keys (personal tokens, vendor console keys) owners must rotate themselves.

integrations: Vendor notes: we requested deletions and log scrubbing; they will confirm within 24-48h.

alisha: Running rotation now, will update ticket with new secret-manager version.

sec-bot: Reminder: This is a required org action. Non-compliance escalates to manager and security.

marco: Thanks everyone. Once you've rotated, reply here with "rotated" and SEC-3301 link. If you need help patching CI or secret syncers, ping @ops-oncall.

alisha: rotated — SEC-3301-12 (new secret-manager version v2026-03-21-01).
